subject: Alignment: evaluation fenceposts, acceptance tests & final close window
messages:
From: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@medsys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: short pilot & evaluation plan

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team was impressed with the inference latency numbers. We have a condensed evaluation window from Aug 17 - Sep 4 and need to be explicit about what ‘pass’ looks like. Can you send a proposed set of success criteria, exit gates, and acceptance tests that tie to our contract milestones?

High-level asks from my side:
- Minimum inference latency targets at 99th percentile (for 512 tokens)
- Token-level cost estimate for our projected query mix (50k tokens/day)
- Examples of fallback/rollover behavior if throughput drops
- Security/compliance artifacts we can share with procurement (SOC2, retention policy)

We need a MAP and a 2-week acceptance sprint plan so procurement has dates to work against.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Lopez
Director, Clinical Partnerships
MedSys Health

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@medsys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: short pilot & evaluation plan

Dana — thanks, this is helpful. I attached a working MAP (MAP-v2.xlsx) and a short runbook below. Quick summary of our proposed acceptance surface and schedule: please review and flag anything that won't work for your signoffs.

Proposed evaluation window and milestones
- Prep & baseline (Aug 10–16): test harness, synthetic load, and warm cache.
- Acceptance sprint (Aug 17–30): 2-week sprint with daily smoke tests + triage.
- Handoff & close (Aug 31–Sep 4): run final pass, collect evidence, procurement sign-off.

Success criteria (high-level) — must all be satisfied to pass:
1) Latency SLO: 99th percentile latency <= 1200ms for 512-token responses under your expected mix
2) Quality: sample concordance >= 88% on the provided prompt set (we'll run pairwise evals)
3) Cost: observed token cost within +/-15% of the predicted baseline in the MAP
4) Reliability: no more than 1 production-level incident (P1/P2) attributable to inference in the sprint window

Exit gates / hard stops
- Fail-fast gate: if 99p latency exceeds 2200ms for two consecutive days during acceptance sprint, we pause and implement mitigations (added capacity / fallback model).
- Quality gate: if concordance falls below 80% on two verification runs, we trigger model rollback to the previous variant.
- Procurement gate: evidence bundle (latency traces, cost report, SOC2 summary) must be uploaded to the shared Drive by Sep 2.

Acceptance tests (examples we will run during the sprint)
- Smoke: 1000 synthetic requests with your production mix, measure 50/95/99p latencies and error rate.
- Stability: 24-hour continuous run at expected qps with KV cache priming, check memory usage and tail latencies.
- Regression: 200 annotated prompts from your set, compute concordance and false-positive cases.
- Fallback validation: simulate 20% capacity drop, validate automatic routing to fallback model within 30s and verify output shape/conformance.

Operational ownership & evidence
- Redwood: test harness scripts, daily latency/cost snapshot, integration with your logging for traces.
- MedSys: provide final prompt set, desired cost targets, and compliance contact for procurement.

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx (working plan), SOC2-summary.pdf (high-level artifacts).

Can we lock the acceptance sprint start for Aug 17? If procurement needs more time we can shift the handoff to Sep 6 but we'd prefer to keep the earlier window to meet Q3 rollout dates.

Thanks — looping Karthik & Marissa to confirm capacity and go/no-go lanes.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@medsys.com>

Cc: procurement@medsys.com
Date: 2026-08-04T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: short pilot & evaluation plan

Jonas — this is excellent and close to what we need. A few comments from the product and procurement teams:

1) Latency: our SRE team is targeting a softer production target of 99p <= 1000ms for 512 tokens. Can you run an optimism run during Aug 10–16 and share traces? If we can get 1000ms under realistic load we’ll mark the latency gate as met.
2) Quality: we need concordance >= 90% for the top-3 answer candidates (not just single-output). Can Redwood run the pairwise eval to report top-3 concordance?
3) Cost: procurement asked for a 30-day rolling cost forecast (current + projected for 50k tokens/day) before they can commit to the MAP. We need that by Aug 12 so they can align billing cycles.
4) Compliance: procurement asked for the full SOC2 control matrix (the summary is helpful but they want the matrix or a contact to request it).

I’m attaching inline comments to MAP-v2.xlsx (see Drive link) and procurement will follow up if they need another artifact.

If you can confirm the optimism run schedule (traces uploaded by Aug 13) and the cost forecast by Aug 12 we will lock Aug 17 as the acceptance start.

Thanks,
Dana
